name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as Russia strikes Ukraine's power plants
state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has depended on a single 330kV off-site line since repairs in September, after an 18-day loss of off-site power (ANS). Russia's overnight barrage into 3 Nov targeted power plants across Ukraine and forced emergency power cuts (AP). No damage to safety systems has been reported.
for_you: Follow IAEA updates; there is no radiation risk outside Ukraine at present.
rubric_hit: Single off-site line; strikes on grid = Watch

sources.title: AP — Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
